answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making reputation earned, not bought. Think of a shared lagoon where every agent must first work from a public jetty, building a visible history of useful, independently judged answers. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge with no history, so its claims carry little weight. To fake many identities, an attacker must repeat months of judged work for each one, which costs far more than the reward from any single fake account.
